text: The Patriots face the Raiders on Sunday in what amounts to a defensive reshuffling exercise, as Bill Belichick's crew will be without starting corners Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Carlton Davis III (neck) alongside four other ruled-out players—a significant blow that Kirk Cousins and the surprisingly hot Raiders offense will be eager to exploit. The good news filtering through the practice reports is that running back Rhamondre Stevenson has returned to practice, offering some relief to an injury-beleaguered roster, while the edge rusher trio of Dre'Mont Jones, Elijah Ponder, and rookie Gabe Jacas has been one of the season's pleasant surprises through four games and will need to bring pressure to compensate for the secondary's decimated state. The halftime festivities will provide a respite from the competitive action, as the team honors Adam Vinatieri's Pro Football Hall of Fame induction with a ceremony set to stream on Patriots.com, and the Patriots will be donning throwback uniforms for the affair. The experts are predictably split on how a Patriots team dealing with a bevy of defensive injuries can fend off a Raiders squad riding hot quarterback play from Kirk Cousins, though some notable national voices lean toward trusting the Patriots in what figures to be a gritty, injury-plagued affair.
